items.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001
items.q: I played with Charlie Parker and Billy Taylor and Miles Davis’ band and I’ve had all kinds of great, wonderful experiences you know, Dizzy Gillespie and all that stuff.

ctx.x: Yeah that was by accident also. Because I always felt that I could see myself up there like a Buddy Rich or a Gene Krupa or some great drummer, with the spotlight on him you know, and all the girls looking at you you know, and that’d be great. So I would take my little allowance you know and go down on 42nd Street, and a Wurlitzer, and take drum lessons on Saturday. And when I got to high school I was going to study the drums. But when I got there — oh Sonny Payne was in that school at that time, and he was like…

had no idea that I would have any kind of career like I’ve had you know. I played with Charlie Parker and Billy Taylor and Miles Davis’ band and I’ve had all kinds of great, wonderful experiences you know, Dizzy Gillespie and all that stuff. So had I thought I probably would have —
Made yourself stay in the band.
